title: Complexe de De Rham à puissance divisée [conférence de 1976 à l’IHÉS] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 11-13). For a simplicial set X_• and a ring k, Grothendieck uses C^{··}_DRpd(X_•, k). This is the simplicial-set analogue of Sullivan's polynomial forms A_PL, but built from divided-power polynomial de Rham complexes. On each simplex Δ^n one takes the divided-power algebra k<t_1..t_n> ⊗ Λ(dt_1..dt_n). It is bigraded by polynomial (divided-power) degree and form degree, with d(t^{[n]}) = t^{[n-1]}dt of bidegree (-1,+1). One then takes the end/limit over the simplices of X_•. Because the divided-power Poincaré lemma holds over any k, the total cohomology is H^*(X,k) with its cup-product. The result is a strictly graded-commutative (with divided powers) integral model of cochains.

On p.11 he asks whether the functor (Hot) → (derived category of DRpd-complexes) gives an equivalence for k = Z. The restriction would be to simply connected types with finitely generated homology, matched against DRpd complexes with H^0 = Z, H^1 = 0 and finitely generated H^i. This is the integral Sullivan problem.

This page (numbered 12) records the state of that programme.
(c) He has tried to recover cohomology operations, Steenrod squares/powers or Whitney-type operations, from the functor C^{··}_DRpd(X_•, -). He has only partial, negative results: the multiplicative structures available on C_DRpd with coefficients like Z/p yield nothing interesting. In modern terms, a strictly commutative (even divided-power) cochain model cannot carry the Steenrod operations, which need E∞/homotopy-coherent commutativity.
(d) Hence one should first develop Sullivan-type minimal models in this integral divided-power setting. The aim is to express the homotopy type of X_• through C^{··}_DRpd(X_•, Z) under finiteness hypotheses. He states he has done nothing in this direction. He has not even proved a Künneth formula C_DRpd(X×Y) ≃ C_DRpd(X) ⊗ C_DRpd(Y). The technical obstruction he names is that C_DRpd(X×Y, k) probably cannot be assumed flat over k{T}, presumably the divided-power polynomial algebra (or bigraded base) over which the complexes are modules.

The next page proposes the remedy of dualizing. One replaces the cochain object by a differential divided-power coalgebra C^{DRpd}_{··}(X, Z) that commutes with all colimits and has base change C_{··}(X,h') = C_{··}(X,h) ⊗ h'. This would allow (b), (c), (d) to be treated without finiteness conditions.
errors: No outright error. The negative finding in (c) is consistent with later knowledge: strictly commutative or divided-power cochain models over Z or F_p cannot detect Steenrod operations. For example, in divided-power algebras x^p = p!γ_p(x) ≡ 0 mod p for even-degree classes, whereas in H^*(CP^∞; F_p) one has x^p ≠ 0. This also suggests the p.11 conjectural equivalence is false as stated.
The Künneth issue is real but stated tentatively ('sans doute'); no argument is given.

ideas.what: Integral polynomial de Rham complex with divided powers for simplicial sets, computing H^*(X,k) for any k
ideas.modern_name: integral/divided-power analogue of Sullivan's A_PL; integral polynomial forms
ideas.usually_credited_to: Cenkl–Porter (tame homotopy, integral polynomial forms, early 1980s); related work by Karoubi
ideas.where_published: Only in this 1976 IHÉS lecture material, as far as I know (unsure)

ideas.what: Attempt to reconstruct Steenrod/Whitney operations from the commutative DRpd model; negative result
ideas.modern_name: obstruction to commutative cochains; necessity of E∞ structure
ideas.usually_credited_to: Steenrod-operations folklore; Mandell (2001 p-adic, 2006 integral E∞ cochains determine finite-type nilpotent homotopy types)

ideas.modern_name: integral minimal models / integral rational-homotopy-type models; schematization of homotopy types

ideas.where_published: Related schematization ideas appear in Pursuing Stacks (1983) and letters; this specific DRpd version not published

ideas.what: Künneth formula for DRpd cochains; flatness obstruction over k{T}

missed.claim: Grothendieck already saw in 1975-76 that a strictly commutative integral (divided-power) de Rham model fails to see Steenrod operations. He concluded that integral Sullivan theory requires more structure: dual coalgebras, then minimal models. This anticipates the later diagnosis (Mandell's E∞ theorem; Toën/Horel binomial-ring models of nilpotent finite-type spaces) and places his DRpd lecture as an early, uncredited stage of the integral schematization problem.
missed.quote: n'ai que des résultats partiels négatifs qui montrent qu'avec des [...] multiplicatifs de C_DRpd*(Z/k) on ne trouve rien d'intéressant
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical priority point for integral models of homotopy types. The divided-power setting (as opposed to binomial rings or E∞) remains a natural comparison case, cf. recent work on derived binomial and divided-power rings.

missed.claim: Divided-power Sullivan minimal models over Z and a Künneth theorem for C_DRpd, explicitly left undone.
missed.quote: Il faudrait donc d'abord [disposer] des modèles minimaux à la Sullivan ... Je n'ai rien fait dans cette direction
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Precisely what such models capture, beyond the known failure for Steenrod operations, is a concrete question related to current derived divided-power / binomial algebra.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a clear, early research agenda on integral rational-homotopy-style models with an honest negative result on Steenrod operations. It foreshadows Mandell and Toën/Horel, but contains no finished new theorem, and integral polynomial forms with divided powers appear later in the literature (Cenkl–Porter).
